gap: No result ChatGPT got states Wh per lb for the 3,000 W-continuous stations: the two 2,048 Wh units carry about 42 Wh/lb (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus 42.1, DJI Power 2000 42.2), while two 3,072 Wh units carry more (Dabbsson 3000L 54.1, Jackery HomePower 3000 51.6), so the Dabbsson's extra 8.1 lb buys 1,024 Wh (126 Wh per added lb).
standout_why: Compared against rvgearlab.com (cited), powerstationsrated.com (cited), truewattlab.com (cited), wattsift.com (cited), powerstations.reviews/jackery-3000 (cited) and outagehouse.com. None states Wh per lb or W per lb: rvgearlab gives no weights at all, and powerstationsrated, wattsift and powerstations.reviews list weight and Wh side by side without dividing. None states the wall-recharge time owed per minute of 3,000 W load. The $/Wh half of this angle is NOT new (standout 0-1 on its own): powerstations.reviews already prints $/Wh for Dabbsson 3000L ($0.33), Pecron F3000LFP ($0.29), ALLPOWERS R3500 ($0.38), EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra ($0.45); rvgearlab prints Dabbsson $0.33; truewattlab prints $/useful Wh for the DELTA 3 Max Plus; ChatGPT's own answer already has minutes at 3,000 W (35 / 52). Caveat: several weights come from rival tables, not maker pages (maker pages returned 429 or had empty spec sections).
decides: It argues against ChatGPT's pick. ChatGPT called the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus the 'best balance of power and portability', but at $1,149 it is $0.56/Wh and 42.1 Wh/lb. The Dabbsson 3000L (3,000 W rated, TT-30) at $969 is $0.32/Wh and 54.1 Wh/lb, and runs about 52 minutes at 3,000 W against about 35. The Pecron F3000LFP at $899 is $0.29/Wh but is a pre-order shipping mid-December. For our rows: ALLPOWERS R3500 through our link ($1,055.12) is $0.333/Wh, third on $/Wh among the units I priced today and second among those without a pre-order notice in what I read; it is in the heavy tier if the 93 lb figure holds (34.1 Wh/lb). BLUETTI Apex 200 is $0.426/Wh through our link and ships mid-February 2027, so it cannot be the pick. I could not read a DJI Power 2000 price, so the desk's 'DJI #1 on price' placement is untested here.

findings.label: Wall-charging time owed per minute of 3,000 W use
findings.value: about 2 minutes on a 1,800 W wall charger per minute at 3,000 W
findings.source_title: PECRON F3000LFP Portable Power Station 3600W 3072Wh PRE-ORDER | Ships Mid Dec
findings.note: Pecron states '1800W AC Charging ... 15A Max'; Dabbsson states 1,800 W AC input for the 3000L (dabbsson.com listing, read 2026-11-27). A 3,000 W load at 85% efficiency draws 3,000 / 0.85 = 3,529 W from the battery; 3,529 / 1,800 = 1.96. Ignores charging losses, so the real figure is slightly higher.

findings.note: Outage House states 2,400 W per household outlet and 3,600 W from the 30 A outlet on the Jackery HomePower 3000. 120 V × 20 A = 2,400 W; 120 V × 30 A = 3,600 W. Not new: ChatGPT's answer already warns that the EcoFlow's outlets are 20 A each.
